Raul (Acme): hey team, running into something weird on embeddings. Our app expects 1536-dim vectors but the API is returning 256-dim vectors for recent requests. Customer noticed lower-cost model used and billing appears to be attributed to a different org. Can you help?

Maya S (Support): sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the exact request you sent (no secrets) and the response headers/body you saw? any project/org headers?

Raul (Acme): here's a sanitized curl we used:

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-ACME123" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "X-Redwood-Org: other-org-987" \n  -d '{"input":"some text"}'
```

Response top lines:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Redwood-Model: text-embed-lite-v1
X-Redwood-Embedding-Dims: 256
{ "data": [{ "embedding": [ /* 256 floats */ ] }] }
```

We never set that org header intentionally — our infra layer injects headers and I think it flipped to another org.

Maya S (Support): thanks — that header explains it. We route embedding model selection using header/project mappings. Will reproduce. Quick Q: what's your expected project id for these requests?

Raul (Acme): project id is `acme-search-01`. Our API key is org-scoped but should map to acme-search-01 by default. The key metadata shows owner_org=acme, owner_project=acme-search-01.

Linh (eng-ml): triage notes: embedding selection precedence is: explicit X-Redwood-Project header > API-key mapped project > X-Redwood-Org header > API-key mapped org default. If a client sends X-Redwood-Org, we route to that org's default embedding profile unless project header is present. From the curl you pasted, `X-Redwood-Org: other-org-987` caused selection of `text-embed-lite-v1` (256 dims).

Jordan (Infra): adding logs from our replay of the request:
```
REQUEST id=rs-91a2 route_eval=start headers={Authorization: sk-prod-ACME123, X-Redwood-Org: other-org-987}
route_eval: project_header=null api_key_project=acme-search-01 org_header=other-org-987 api_key_org=acme -> selected_org=other-org-987 selected_project=other-org-default -> selected_model=text-embed-lite-v1 dims=256
```

That line shows the bug: for org-scoped keys we should not let an unrelated X-Redwood-Org override the api_key_project mapping. We have a precedence enforcement bug in the header-mapper.

Maya S (Support): repro steps for support engineers: 1) Send request with a valid key that maps to a project, but add a different X-Redwood-Org header. 2) Observe `X-Redwood-Model` and `X-Redwood-Embedding-Dims` in response. 3) Check `route_eval` logs for `selected_project`.

Sample validation curl (sanitized):
```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-ACME123" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "X-Redwood-Project: acme-search-01" \n  -d '{"input":"test"}'
```

If you include `X-Redwood-Project` explicitly we correctly pick the large model. If you pass only `X-Redwood-Org` for another org we hit the smaller one.

Jordan (Infra): mitigation/actions: we pushed a hotfix to the header-mapper to enforce project mapping when an api-key maps to a project (release note: header-mapper v2.34.1). For immediate customer workaround: remove the stray `X-Redwood-Org` header or explicitly set `X-Redwood-Project: acme-search-01`. We'll also rotate and audit any header-injecting infra to avoid accidental insertion.

Priya (Billing): heads-up on billing impact: since the requests billed against `other-org-987` (cheaper model), Acme undercharged. We should credit Acme for the difference for the affected time window. Maya, can you collect request ids / time range (Raul said this started ~2026-03-10 14:00 UTC)? We'll run a reconciliation and issue a credit if warranted.

Maya S (Support): noted — Raul, can you confirm approximate start time and sample request ids if you have them? We'll attach credits and escalate to finance.

Raul (Acme): start ≈ 2026-03-10T14:05Z, most impacted between 14:05–15:30. I pulled a few request ids: rs-7f1a2c, rs-7f1b33.

Maya S (Support): thanks. Steps we'll take: 1) infra already released a hotfix to enforce precedence. 2) Billing will run a delta calc and propose credits (Priya on it). 3) Eng-ML will add a server-side diagnostic header to surface dim mismatches to clients in future.

Linh (eng-ml): follow-up: we'll add a transient header `X-Redwood-Embed-Dim-Warn: expected=1536 actual=256` when the API detects the api-key maps to a project with a different expected embedding dims than the final selected model. That should make silent misrouting visible to clients immediately. Planning rollout in next 24h.

Jordan (Infra): also adding an internal alert when an API key that maps to a project results in a different selected_project for >0.1% of requests in a 1h window.

Priya (Billing): starting the audit for the 14:00–15:30 window and will DM Maya with preliminary numbers.

Raul (Acme): thanks team — can confirm removing the stray header locally fixes it. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Maya S (Support): closing loop: we created ticket RDW-9832. We'll update here when credits applied and the diagnostic header is live. :lock: :white_check_mark: 

deploy-bot: hotfix header-mapper v2.34.1 deployed to prod in us-west-2 at 2026-03-11T02:17:10Z (canary 100%).

Raul (Acme): awesome, thanks everyone :raised_hands:
